question.problem: A surface $S$ is defined by $z=f(x,y).$ The curve $C$ is the intersection of $S$ with the plane $x=2.$ Given that the point $P$ with $y$-coordinate $\frac{\pi }{4}$ lies on $C$, and that ${f}_{y}=y\operatorname{sin}⁡(xy-\frac{\pi }{3})$, find the slope of the tangent to $C$ at $P.$
question.worked_solution:
The curve $C$ is the intersection of the surface $z=f(x,y)$ with the plane $x=2.$ Hence, the slope of the tangent to the curve $C$ at the point where $y=\frac{\pi }{4}$ will be given by the partial derivative ${f}_{y}(2,\frac{\pi }{4}).$ 

To get the slope, we evaluate the partial derivative ${f}_{y}(x,y)$ at $(2,\frac{\pi }{4}):$ 

$$
\begin{aligned}{f}_{y}(2,\frac{\pi }{4}) & =\frac{\pi }{4}\cdot \operatorname{sin}⁡(2\cdot \frac{\pi }{4}-\frac{\pi }{3}) \\  & =\frac{\pi }{4}\operatorname{sin}⁡(\frac{\pi }{6}) \\  & =\frac{\pi }{4}\cdot \frac{1}{2} \\  & =\frac{\pi }{8}\end{aligned}
$$
